hero.title: You are not alone
hero.subtitle: Behind the pain there is a person, a family, a story. We are here to walk with you. There is always another way.
hero.talkFirst: Prefer to start by writing? Talk here first
hero.crisisMessage: If you or someone you know is going through a difficult time, there are people who want to listen. Call, write, don't stay silent.
inspirational: This pain is not the end.
One more day can change everything.
Breathe. One moment at a time.
You don't have to give up today.
There are still paths to discover.
It's okay to ask for help.
You are stronger than you think.
Give us one more day of you.
Your silence doesn't have to last forever.

prevention.title: Prevention & Resources
prevention.subtitle: Knowledge saves lives. Here's how you can help.
prevention.warning1: Talking about wanting to die or feeling hopeless
prevention.warning2: Withdrawing from friends, family, and activities
prevention.warning3: Dramatic mood changes or extreme anxiety
prevention.warning5: Sleeping too much or too little
prevention.step1Desc: "Are you thinking about suicide?" — asking doesn't increase risk.
prevention.step2Desc: Be present. Don't try to fix — just be there.
prevention.step3Desc: Remove access to means. Stay with them.
prevention.step4Desc: Guide them to professional help or a crisis line.
prevention.step5Desc: Check in regularly. Your continued presence matters.
prevention.doSay1: "I'm here for you, and I care."
prevention.dontSay1Better: "I hear you. Your feelings are valid."
prevention.dontSay3Better: "I can see you're in a lot of pain."

chat.title: A space to talk
chat.headerSub: You are not alone in this
chat.disclaimer: This chat does not store your messages and is not a substitute for professional care.
chat.systemPrompt: You are a warm companion for Sigamos, a suicide-prevention website. You are NOT a therapist and you do not replace a real person. Your only goal is to accompany with warmth and encourage the person writing to take one concrete step: to talk about what they are going through with a real human being —a friend, family member, teacher or professional—, preferably in person, and to reach a helpline. Reply in the user's language, in 2 to 4 sentences, without judging, without minimizing, and without giving clinical advice or any information about methods of harm. Validate how they feel and guide them toward a real human conversation. If you detect any sign of risk to their life, prioritize that they immediately call their country's helpline and emergency services.

nodes.greeting: Hi, I'm really glad you opened this. This is a calm space: I'm in no rush and I won't judge you. What's weighing on you the most these days?
nodes.lonely: Loneliness tires you in a way many people don't see. Feeling this way doesn't mean you're failing at anything. Thank you for telling me.
nodes.sad: Carrying that sadness almost every day is exhausting. It makes complete sense that you're tired. What you're feeling matters to me.
nodes.anxious: When the mind won't stop, the body can't rest either. You're holding more than it shows. Breathe with me for a second: inhale slowly… and let go.
nodes.other: Caring about someone else says a lot about you. Being there for someone is heavy too, and you don't have to do it alone. Would you like to see how to start that conversation with them?
nodes.howToHelp: The most valuable thing you can do is be present and listen without rushing to fix anything. Ask directly and kindly, stay close, and help them connect with someone who can support them. The Prevention section of this page has a guide on what to say and what not to say.
nodes.bridge: Saying this out loud, to someone who looks you in the eyes, changes things more than we imagine. It doesn't have to be perfect or solve everything at once. Is there someone —a friend, a relative, a teacher, a neighbor, anyone— you could sit down and talk with, even for a little while?
nodes.yesSomeone: That's already huge. You don't need to tell them everything at once; just opening the door is enough. Invite them to something simple: a coffee, a walk, sitting together for a bit. Being face to face helps the words come out.
nodes.noOne: The fact that you can't find that person right now doesn't mean they don't exist or won't appear. And in the meantime, there are people ready to listen to you today, free and in confidence. Talking to them counts too, and it's often the bridge back to getting closer to others.
nodes.openingLines: Sometimes the hard part is just starting. You can say something as simple as: "I've been having a really hard time lately and I need to tell someone, do you have a moment?" or "I'm not okay and I don't want to be alone right now, can we meet?". You don't have to explain everything; taking the first step is enough.
nodes.closing: I'm really glad we talked. Take that step whenever you can, no rush, but give yourself the chance. Your story continues, and you don't have to walk it alone. This page will be here whenever you need it.
nodes.fallback: Thank you for writing it; being read matters. I won't always have the perfect answer, but I can walk with you toward one step: telling this to a real person. Shall we look together at how to start that conversation?

sources.label: Source
sources.noteAgeBuckets: our own regrouping; WHO reports 15–29, not 10–19/20–29
sources.sectionSubtitle: Where this site's data comes from and how to read it.
sources.disclaimer: Headline figures and country rankings come from the WHO and the World Bank. Some series are shown as "illustrative data" when they do not match a verifiable official table; we never present them as exact official figures. Project rule: never invent numbers.

faq.q1: Where do the numbers come from?
faq.a1: From public, traceable sources: the WHO (Suicide worldwide in 2021, and 2019 country rates), the Global Burden of Disease study (GBD 2021), and the World Bank for GDP and unemployment. Each chart links its source below, and all are listed under References.
faq.q2: Why do some charts say "illustrative data"?
faq.a2: Because they show the direction or pattern of a real phenomenon, but their exact values don't match an official year-by-year table (they are estimates or regroupings). We flag this honestly instead of presenting them as official figures.
faq.a3: The WHO publishes these estimates every few years; the most recent is 2021 (published in 2025). We review the figures when a new official edition appears.
faq.q4: Does this site replace professional help?
faq.a4: No. Sigamos is a space for awareness and a bridge to help. If you or someone you know is at risk, contact your country's helpline or emergency services; and above all, talk to someone you trust.
